title: Reboiler

introduction.definition: A reboiler supplies heat to the bottom of a distillation column to boil part of the bottom liquid. The vapour produced rises up the column and drives the separation. In a kettle reboiler, the liquid floods a horizontal tube bundle inside an enlarged shell; steam or hot oil inside the tubes boils the liquid. Vapour leaves from the top; unvaporised liquid spills over a weir and leaves as bottom product.
applications: Distillation columns in refineries and chemical plants
Duties with wide boiling ranges or high vaporisation fraction
key_points: Kettle = pool boiling around a submerged bundle
Heat duty sets the column boil-up
introduction.summary: A kettle reboiler supplies the vapour that drives a distillation column. Liquid from the column bottom floods a horizontal tube bundle inside an enlarged shell; steam or hot oil inside the tubes boils part of the liquid. Vapour rises to the column through the top nozzles; the remaining liquid spills over a weir and leaves as bottom product.

working_principle.characteristic_curve: Boiling heat flux vs wall superheat (pool-boiling curve): duty rises steeply with ΔT up to the critical heat flux — designs stay well below it.

foundation: Support on saddles or structure designed for the operating and full-of-water (hydro-test) weight; bolt one saddle and slot the other for thermal expansion.
alignment: Level the unit (or set the specified slope for drainage); leave tube-bundle pull-out space equal to the bundle length.
piping: Connect nozzles without forcing (check allowable nozzle loads); fit vents at high points and drains at low points on both sides.
Steam-heated units: install a steam trap or level-controlled drain and a vacuum breaker so condensate cannot back up.
commissioning: Hydro-test both sides per code; vent air; introduce the cold fluid first, then the hot fluid gradually to avoid thermal shock.

routine.task: Monitor steam flow vs boil-up and condensate drainage.

periodic.task: Trend U-value; check for tube leaks (process in condensate).

overhaul.task: Pull and clean the bundle; inspect tubes (eddy current); replace gaskets.

lubrication: No lubrication for the static parts — lubricate valve stems, rotating parts and drives per maker.

symptoms: Falling duty, higher steam pressure needed

safety: Relief protection for blocked outlet and tube rupture cases (API 521); isolate and drain before opening.

script.narration: This module introduces the Reboiler.
A reboiler supplies heat to the bottom of a distillation column to boil part of the bottom liquid.
The vapour produced rises up the column and drives the separation.
In a kettle reboiler, the liquid floods a horizontal tube bundle inside an enlarged shell; steam or hot oil inside the tubes boils the liquid.
Typical applications include distillation columns in refineries and chemical plants; gas plants (amine regenerators, stabilisers); duties with wide boiling ranges or high vaporisation fraction.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Kettle Shell (enlarged vapour space) & Bundle Neck, Channel Head with Pass Partition & Tubesheet.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.

script.narration: How the Reboiler works.
Bottom liquid from the column enters the kettle shell.
Steam enters the channel and condenses inside the U-tubes.
The submerged tube bundle boils the liquid; vapour bubbles rise.
The weir keeps the bundle flooded; overflow liquid leaves as product.
Vapour returns to the column through the top nozzles.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.

video_tutorials.title: Reboiler — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Reboiler.
Monitor steam flow vs boil-up and condensate drainage.
Trend U-value; check for tube leaks (process in condensate).
Pull and clean the bundle; inspect tubes (eddy current); replace gaskets.
Watch for fouling of the bundle: falling duty, higher steam pressure needed. Common cause: polymerisation, salts, coke.
Watch for condensate backing up: low duty, hammering. Common cause: faulty trap, low steam pressure (stall).
Watch for liquid entrainment: liquid carried to column. Common cause: vapour space too small, foaming.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
